The closest match is “Sympathetic Framing: Evaluating AI Alignment across Sociodemographic Groups” by Haran Shani-Narkiss, Michael Fire, and Oren Tsur [1]. It empirically evaluates whether LLMs align with human emotional perceptions of sympathy in news headlines about political/geopolitical conflicts, and reports that alignment varies across demographic subgroups (age, gender, education, prior geopolitical knowledge, and predispositions), with some statistically significant differences despite broadly aligned performance across groups [1].

If you instead meant social-norm or broader societal alignment using socio-demographic context, “Mapping how LLMs debate societal issues when shadowing human personality traits, sociodemographics and social media behavior” provides a synthetic corpus designed for audits of bias, social sensitivity, and alignment across sociodemographic attributes in prompted LLM discourse [4]. “Group Alignment-Induced Sycophancy” differs by focusing on how group alignment can shift sycophantic behavior in a two-sided way across multiple demographic groups [3].
